title: Deformation space of a closed section
statement:
Use the coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions] and the situation of [def-pur-section-invariant]: $B,V$ are finite-type $k$-schemes, $g:V\to B$ is smooth, separated and of finite type, and $s:B\hookrightarrow V$ is a closed section, $g\circ s=\mathrm{id}_B$. No constant relative dimension is imposed. Affine space is [def-sbc-affine-space], and fibre products are [def-pc-fibre-product]. The deformation to the normal cone of the section is the actual scheme
$$
D_sV=\operatorname{Bl}_{s(B)\times\{0\}}(V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B)
\setminus\widetilde{V\times_B\{0\}},
$$
where the blow-up is [def-nagata-global-blowup] and the tilde is the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], not just a topological closure. Write $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_V\to s_*\mathcal O_B)$ for the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$, with $I=\mathcal I(U)$, the inverse image of $U$ in $D_sV$ is
$$
\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t],\qquad R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}],
$$
the subalgebra generated by $R[t]$ and all $f/t$ with $f\in I$. The spectrum and its contravariant maps are [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. These charts specify the maps
$$
\widetilde g:D_sV\longrightarrow\mathbf A^1_B,\qquad
\widetilde s:\mathbf A^1_B\longrightarrow D_sV:
$$
$\widetilde g$ is the blow-up projection followed by projection to $\mathbf A^1_B$, and $\widetilde s$ is induced on the displayed chart by the augmentation $R[t,I/t]\to(R/I)[t]$, $r\mapsto\bar r$, $t\mapsto t$, $f/t\mapsto0$. They satisfy $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde s=\mathrm{id}$; $\widetilde g$ is smooth separated of finite type and $\widetilde s$ is a closed immersion [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $\omega_{\widetilde g}=R\widetilde g^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B}$ as in [def-pur-section-invariant]. The family object is the actual derived pullback
$$
F=L\widetilde s^*\omega_{\widetilde g}
=C(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)
\in\operatorname{Pic}\bigl(D^b_{ctf}(\mathbf A^1_B,\Lambda)\bigr).
$$
The derived operations and the Picard groupoid have precisely the meaning of [def-pur-section-invariant]; in particular this asserts tensor invertibility and finite Tor amplitude, with no chosen orientation. At finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ this is the finite family; the other coefficient stages use exactly the transports of [def-pur-conventions]. Here $\Lambda_T$ is the coefficient unit of [def-pur-conventions]: $A_T$ at finite level, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ at integral level, and its rationalized or common-stage image at field levels. The integral bounded-constructible and finite-Tor conditions use single intervals uniform in all finite reductions, as specified there.

proof.text: Construct the global blow-up and strict transform using [def-nagata-global-blowup] and [def-nagata-strict-transform]. The gluing data and local models [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data] and [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model] reduce the calculation to affine charts. A field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, hence is Noetherian. Finite-type $k$-schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so on a finite affine cover the section ideal is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For an arbitrary affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$ the ideal $I=\mathcal I(U)$ is finitely generated too: each $x\in U$ lies in a chart $U_j$ of that cover, and [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both] gives $a\in R$ and $b\in\mathcal O_V(U_j)$ with $x\in D_U(a)=D_{U_j}(b)$; by quasi-coherence [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], $I_a=\mathcal I(D_U(a))=\mathcal I(U_j)_b$ is generated by the images of finitely many generators of $\mathcal I(U_j)$. Finitely many such $a$ cover the quasi-compact $U$, hence generate the unit ideal of $R$, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-of-localization-span] shows that $I$ is finitely generated. The centre has affine ideal $(I,t)$, is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and is affine, quasi-compact and a finite-presentation centre by [def-weil-closed-immersion], [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] and [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The schematic closure is computed by [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure] and [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc].

source.place: Tags 01OG, 0804, 080D; affine centre and schematic closure setup

proof.text: For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq V$, with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ finitely generated by step 1, apply [lem-pur-dnc-affine-blowup-complement] to the blow-up centre $(I,t)$. It gives the $t$-chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$, the $f_i$-charts $\operatorname{Spec}R[I/f_i][v]$ with $v=t/f_i$, the strict-transform equation $v=0$, and the identification of its complement with the displayed $t$-chart. These identifications localize in $R$, so they glue to the actual deformation open.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; explicit affine chart calculation

proof.text: The projection to $\mathbf A^1_B$ is the restriction of the blow-up projection. Write $A=R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$. Every element has a unique finite Laurent expression $\sum_j a_jt^j$: uniqueness holds for Laurent polynomials over any ring, including rings with zero divisors. The coefficient condition for membership in $A$ is $a_j\in I^{-j}$ for $j<0$, with unrestricted coefficients for $j\geq0$. Indeed the generators have this property, it is preserved by products and sums, and each element of $I^r$ is a finite sum of products of $r$ elements of $I$. Define $\epsilon(\sum_j a_jt^j)=\sum_{j\geq0}\bar a_jt^j\in(R/I)[t]$. It is additive. For multiplicativity, a product term involving a negative exponent has a coefficient in $I$; if its resulting exponent is nonnegative it reduces to zero, and otherwise it is discarded. Terms involving only nonnegative exponents multiply by ordinary reduction modulo $I$. Thus $\epsilon$ is a ring map, sends every $f/t$ to zero, and is surjective because it contains all reduced constants and $t$. The affine-spectrum functor of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the surjective-ring-map criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion] give $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)[t]\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$. These formulas agree after localizing $R$, hence agree on affine refinements of overlaps and glue to $\widetilde s$. The inverse image of each deformation chart is precisely $s^{-1}(U)\times\mathbf A^1$; these charts cover the target and their inverse images are affine. This proves closedness globally by the same affine criterion. The map fixes all base functions and $t$, so $\widetilde g\circ\widetilde s=\mathrm{id}$. Lean realization of the intrinsic wrappers: use the already proved Scheme.Hom.deformationSpaceSection_deformationSpaceProj for the actual Rees section. Associativity gives purityDncIntrinsicSection_over, and Over morphism extensionality gives purityDncIntrinsicSection_comp_map. No repeated affine augmentation proof is needed.

source.place: Definition: the displayed projection and section; explicit augmentation of the deformation algebra

proof.text: Construct etale coordinates of the pair near each point $s(b)$. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], after restricting to affine neighbourhoods, $g$ factors as an etale map $e:W\to\mathbf A^d_{B'}$ followed by projection, with $b\in B'$ and $s(b)\in W$. Shrink $B'$ into $s^{-1}(W)$ so the whole restricted section lands in $W$. Subtract the $d$ coordinate functions of $e\circ s$; translation by these functions is an automorphism of affine space, so the translated etale map sends $s$ to the zero section. Put $P=W\times_{\mathbf A^d_{B'}}B'$. Its projection $P\to B'$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The map $e$ is separated: on the initial affine neighbourhoods it is affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target], hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]; restriction and base change restrict its closed diagonal. Thus $P\to B'$ is separated. The induced section $B'\to P$ is open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Remove the other open-and-closed component of $P$ from $W$; it is closed in $W$, since $P$ is the inverse image of the closed zero section. After this restriction $e^{-1}(0)=s(B')$ as closed subschemes. Refine again around $s(b)$ to an affine open and shrink $B'$ to a principal affine neighbourhood in its inverse image under $s$; the restriction of that affine open is again principal affine, so both schemes remain affine. Such restrictions preserve etaleness by [def-weil-etale-morphism], since the condition is affine-local. We obtain affine coordinates $B'=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\to R$ etale, with the actual section ideal $I=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)R$. Closedness and restriction here use precisely the affine quotient criterion of [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the diagonal definition of [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Clause (2), coordinates of the closed section; expanded using Stacks Tags 054L, 02GO, 024T, 01KT, 01S8

proof.text: On the affine pair chart from step 4, let $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\subset C=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ and $I=JR$. The affine calculation [lem-pur-dnc-etale-rees-chart] identifies the actual chart $R[t,I/t]$ with the étale base change of $A[t,u_1,\ldots,u_d]$ along $x_i\mapsto t u_i$, and gives smoothness of its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$.

source.place: Clause (2), calculation $x_i=t u_i$ and flat tensor injection

proof.text: The identity $f=t(f/t)$ puts every point over $t=0$ in the section neighbourhoods of step 4, so these charts cover the zero fibre. After inverting $t$, $R[t,I/t][t^{-1}]=R[t,t^{-1}]$, giving $V\times_B\mathbf G_{m,B}$; its projection is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). Smoothness is affine-local by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and the local coordinate number may vary between charts, so the projection is smooth everywhere. No geometric DNC theorem is used.

source.place: Clause (2), zero-fibre coverage and punctured chart

proof.text: The chart description also makes $h:D_sV\to V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$ affine by [pqf-lem-affine-local-target]: the inverse image of $U\times\mathbf A^1=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$. Each algebra is finitely generated over $R[t]$, with generators $f_1/t,\ldots,f_m/t$. Thus $h$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). The projection $p:V\times_B\mathbf A^1_B\to\mathbf A^1_B$ is separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to the stated $g$. The composite $\widetilde g=ph$ is of finite type: over each affine target choose finitely many affine charts for $p$, then finitely many for $h$ above those, and compose the finite sets of algebra generators. Its diagonal factors as the closed diagonal of $h$ followed by the base change of the closed diagonal of $p$; a base change of a surjective ring map is surjective, and a composition of surjections is surjective, so these maps are closed immersions by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is precisely separatedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finally $\mathbf A^1_B$ and $D_sV$ are finite type over $k$: on a finite affine cover of $B$ use the polynomial algebra $R[t]$, and compose with the finite-type map just established. All domain hypotheses of the section-invariant definition are now verified. The existing purityDncDomain declaration in Sheaf.Paper.PurityDncFamily already states exactly the six geometric domain clauses of purityDncIntrinsicDomain: the bases, sources, projection and underlying section are definitionally equal. The intrinsic wrapper uses that declaration directly; the geometric proof obligations of steps 1-7 remain in purityDncDomain, rather than being duplicated in the intrinsic module.

source.place: Well-definedness of the displayed exceptional inverse image: separated finite-type domain

proof.text: Apply [def-pur-section-invariant] to the actual pair $(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)$ constructed in steps 1–3. Steps 4–7 give precisely its smooth, separated, finite-type and finite-type-over-$k$ hypotheses, and step 3 gives the closed section and its identity. Define $F$ to be that node's actual derived pullback $C(\widetilde g,\widetilde s)=L\widetilde s^*R\widetilde g^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_B}$. Its tensor-invertibility and membership in $D^b_{ctf}$ are exactly the final assertion of that node, including its specified higher coefficient stages. This supplies the claimed object of the Picard groupoid. No choice from an existence theorem is used in its underlying data, and no purity orientation is added. More explicitly, [def-pur-conventions] uses the small pro-etale site and the unit $A_T$, $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$, or its rationalized/common-stage image at the respective coefficient stages. Its exceptional inverse image is defined for separated finite-type morphisms between finite-type $k$-schemes; steps 4–7 and the finite-type base $\mathbf A^1_B$ verify exactly that domain. No absolute separatedness of $B$ or $V$ is needed. At integral coefficients the boundedness and Tor intervals are uniform in all finite reductions. The conventions name operations only; the tensor-invertibility assertion used here comes from [def-pur-section-invariant], not from the conventions. No twist tensor comparison or exceptional-adjoint admissibility datum is used. In Lean install the base finite-type and quasi-compact instances, the smooth projection and closed section instances from purityDncIntrinsicDomain, and the existing purityDncCompactifiable instance. Separatedness and quasi-compactness of the projection are the published deformationSpaceProj instances. Apply PurityFiniteSetting.sectionInvariantIntrinsic_invertible with the published deformationSpaceSection_deformationSpaceProj identity. Its family object is definitionally purityDncIntrinsicFamily, with the identical compactification instance; no chosen inverse or tensor comparison needs to be transported.
